comments.body:
## Phase 1 — ROOT CAUSE PROVEN (rebar-debug). Read-only; escalating (infra) — no fix auto-applied.

**Verdict: NOT a reversion of 3a52. A NEW persistent root-disk consumer (the MCP blue-green image family, added after 3a52 closed) plus an insufficient image-retirement path holds root at a ~78–82% floor, so ordinary review/build transients cross the 85% alarm. This is a defect (disk-size-blind image accumulation), but the remediation is INFRA — escalated, not auto-applied.**

### What is filling the root fs (host `i-00880b2c7f13527c5`, read-only via SSM + CloudWatch)
- Root `/` = `/dev/nvme0n1p1` 30 GiB, **23 GiB used / 76%** at time of probe (recovered). `/var` = 24 GiB of 26 GiB under `/`; **`/var/lib/docker` = 15 GiB** is the dominant occupant.
- `docker system df`: **Images 20, 6.78 GB (4.84 GB reclaimable); Build Cache 146 entries, 5.33 GB (all reclaimable)** → ~10 GB reclaimable docker garbage sitting on a 30 GiB root.
- **17 `compose-mcp:<sha>` per-release tagged images (~544–563 MB each) but only 1 live mcp container** (`rebar-mcp-5c28ce66bbfd`, healthy). → ~16 ORPHANED tagged images (~9 GB) whose containers are already gone.
- `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots` absent on host — the gate snapshot store lives inside the container overlay (small, janitor-managed); it is NOT the filler.

### Why the disk never drains (the persistent floor)
- Autodeploy's pressure-reclaim `prune_docker_caches()` (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:328-343`) runs `docker builder prune --keep-storage 5GB` (keeps 5 GB by design — build cache measured 5.33 GB, i.e. pinned at the keep-floor) + `docker image prune -f` (**dangling only, no `-a`**). Its own comment (`:320-326`): *"TAGGED images are never touched here … reclaimed at RETIRE instead — mcp_retire_image."*
- `mcp_retire_image` / `mcp_retire_sweep` (`:474-486`, `:603-632`) remove a `compose-mcp:<sha>` image **only at the moment its container is reaped**, and there is **no reconciliation of orphaned tags** (a tag whose container is already gone is never revisited). Any image whose removal is missed/failed at reap ("still referenced, or already gone" → `:486`) leaks permanently → the observed 16 orphans.

### Runtime proof (in-window, 08-29 17:00 → 08-30 17:00 PDT bucket)
- `root_disk_used_percent` (Maximum @300s): persistent **~78–82% floor** with spikes to 84–98% (peak 98% @ 08-28 01:50); 6 OK→ALARM flaps match the ticket. In the 3a52 era this volume reclaimed to **48%** — the floor has risen ~30 pts.
- **`disk_pressure_prunes` = 77** (autodeploy pressure-prune firing near-continuously) yet **`disk_pressure_persists` = 18** (`AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE_PERSISTS`, `autodeploy.sh:401`) — reclaim ran and recovered nothing, because the reclaimable bytes are tagged images the prune spares.
- **`mcp_retire_cap` = 37** (`AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP`, `:632`) — the retire sweep repeatedly hit its container cap during the busy window and declined to force-kill draining containers, backing up image retirement.

### Why it regressed (timeline)
- 2026-08-19: 3a52 janitor watermark fix landed (`6a4fd2fbb0`) — **still intact on main; not reverted.** RC-A blob-sharing (`b7a4994742c1`) and the byte-total backstop (`8a1ce463d950`) also landed. None of these manage docker images.
- **2026-08-25: `fd4a-4e91-f179-4932` added the rebar-mcp HTTP service to the box** (`8297083532a3`) + blue-green mcp autodeploy target (`2a0a4b19f2ab`) — a **second ~550 MB/deploy tagged-image family on the same 30 GiB root**, the new filler.
- 2026-08-28: `9bc0-1200-1451-44bb` (`6546114de21a` "Reclaim tagged mcp images and prove it") added `mcp_retire_image` retire-at-reap + measurement. **Insufficient**: retire-at-reap-only with no orphan-tag reconciliation → 17 tags accumulated again by 08-30.

### Defect attribution (`caused_by`)
- **Primary `caused_by` → `fd4a-4e91-f179-4932`** (link recorded): it created the obligation — a second per-deploy blue-green image family on the 30 GiB root immediately after the 3a52 P1 disk incident, without provisioning volume/retention to keep pace. A reviewer of fd4a could plausibly have caught this.
- **Also implicated: `9bc0-1200-1451-44bb`** (the tagged-image retirement it shipped is the live leak — retire-at-reap-only, no orphan reconciliation). Class: regression/insufficient-fix of a prior P1 bugfix. The `caused_by` link to 9bc0 was **gate-refused** ("no commit referencing it" — a false negative; `6546114de21a` on main carries `rebar-ticket: 9bc0-…`). Per policy I did **not** `--force`; recording it here in prose.

### Root vs. data disk — independent, NOT a shared cause
Root `/` = 30 GiB `nvme0n1p1` (docker images). `/var/gerrit` = **separate 50 GiB `nvme1n1`, 13% used** (5a05, recovered — that was investigation evidence on the data volume). Different volumes, different fillers.

### Is the LLM-Review fail-close correct?
**Yes — defensible, leave as-is.** ENOSPC on root would corrupt clones/verdicts; failing closed on ≥85% root is correct, not an over-broad trigger. **Do not change gate behavior.**

### Remediation is INFRA — ESCALATED (not auto-applied), options + blast radius
1. **Harden retirement to reconcile orphaned tags** — in `mcp_retire_sweep`, after reaps, remove every `compose-mcp:<sha>` tag that is not the live image / bare build tag (`docker images compose-mcp` minus the in-use ref), not only the just-reaped container's image. *Blast radius:* `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` + `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_*`; changes host image lifecycle; realized only on deploy. Reversible.
2. **One-time reclaim now** — remove the ~16 orphaned `compose-mcp:<sha>` images (~9 GB) / `docker image prune -a` for non-live tags. *Blast radius:* immediate host mutation; frees ~9 GB → ~48% used. Must not remove the live image or `:prev` rollback lifeline.
3. **Give the 30 GiB root headroom** — resize root gp3, or relocate `/var/lib/docker` (or the mcp image family) to the 50 GiB data volume (13% used). *Blast radius:* infra/terraform + docker daemon reconfig; larger change.
4. **Lower `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP`** below 5 GB. *Blast radius:* slower rebuilds; small.

Options 1–4 are all infra/deploy changes → per the debug directive I stop at Phase 1 and hand the design decision to the operator. No RED→GREEN performed; no host mutation performed.

BEFORE -> AFTER:
- df -h /: 23G used / 76% (7.3G avail) -> 19G used / 62% (12G avail).
- docker system df: Images 6.783GB (4.842GB reclaimable) -> 3.304GB; Build Cache 5.328GB -> 0B.
- CloudWatch alarm rebar-root-disk-pressure: ALARM -> OK. LLM-Review fail-close deadlock cleared (unblocks in-flight changes 2451/2449).

Note: root settled at 62% (not the ~50% aspiration) because the remaining ~19G is baseline OS + tickets store + the two preserved mcp images + running containers; reaching ~50% would require the DEFERRED capacity options (root resize / relocate docker / lower BUILD_CACHE_KEEP) or dropping the rollback image — neither in scope. 62% sits well below the 85% flap band with 12G headroom (was 7.3G). Part B (durable orphan-reconciliation fix) proceeds next.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Part B — durable fix (Option 1), Phase 2 for e4f3. Pushed to Gerrit as change 2454 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2454), RED->GREEN under the /rebar-debug protocol. Fresh worktree off origin/main (5c28ce66bbfd); all cmds run with the worktree venv first on PATH. NO --force anywhere.

Root cause (proven, Phase 1): mcp_retire_image (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh) removes a compose-mcp:<sha> image ONLY at the reap of a live-tracked container; a per-release tag whose container was already reaped (or never tracked on this box) leaks forever — `docker image prune` without -a never touches a tagged image. Once the mcp blue-green family (fd4a) landed as a SECOND image family on the 30GiB root, the leak re-filled root and re-tripped rebar-root-disk-pressure, fail-closing LLM-Review. Regression of 3a52 (whose snapshot-GC watermark fix is intact — this is a NEW consumer, not a reversion).

Fix: new mcp_reconcile_orphans, invoked from mcp_retire_sweep (runs on BOTH the active-deploy and the no-op tick, after the reap loop). It enumerates mcp image tags newest-first and retires true orphans, PRESERVING blue-green rollback: the LIVE backend image AND the immediately-previous release (newest non-live <sha> tag) are always kept, plus the bare build tag / :latest / :prev. Removal via `docker image rm` WITHOUT -f (daemon still-referenced refusal is an independent backstop); fails SAFE (touches nothing) if the live image can't be identified.

RED->GREEN evidence:
- RED first: added test_orphaned_per_release_tags_with_no_container_are_reconciled + test_reconcile_never_retires_live_or_immediately_previous (the live+previous preservation invariant is its own test case), plus a `docker images` model + _seed_image helper in the blue-green harness. Ran before implementing -> FAILED (cmds=[]; no reconciliation existed).
- GREEN after implementing: both new tests pass. Full related suite GREEN: tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py + test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py + tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py + test_observability_disk_pressure.py = 79 passed.
- make lint PASS (ruff + format + shellcheck + all repo gates); make typecheck PASS (mypy, 718 files, no issues).

Commit 627faccae8df: `rebar-ticket: e4f3-1661-2319-4a76` trailer + DCO Signed-off-by + Change-Id I39cdfefd; `rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD` = OK. caused_by fd4a retained.

Not closing e4f3 until change 2454 is Verified +1 (per the git-workflow policy) and reclaimed root keeps LLM-Review healthy.

comments.body:
CLOSED (regression; caused_by fd4a). Durable fix landed.

- Gerrit change 2454 MERGED as commit 627faccae8df on main.
  - LLM-Review +1 (SATISFIED) and Verified +1 (SATISFIED) on PS3.
  - PS2's blocking finding (timestamp-based "immediately-previous" selection with a second-granularity CreatedAt sort + random-sha tiebreak) is resolved: the rollback target is now identified by RECORDED DEPLOY ORDER (`$STATE_DIR/mcp-previous-sha`, written at cutover with the OUTGOING live sha), not by a build timestamp. Reconcile preserves exactly {live, recorded-previous}, and FAILS SAFE (removes nothing) when the live image is unidentifiable OR when no previous release has been recorded yet.
  - 2 residual LLM-Review comments on PS3 are advisory `(tests)` coverage nits (guard-4 daemon-refusal backstop; the cutover same-sha guard). Non-blocking: submit_requirements showed No-Unresolved-Comments = NOT_APPLICABLE, unresolved_comment_count = 0. Left as fast-follow rather than churn the +1.

- Root disk stays healthy post-merge: CloudWatch `rebar-root-disk-pressure` = OK (latest datapoint 77%, below the 85% threshold). LLM-Review is unblocked (2454 itself earned LLM-Review +1), confirming the fail-closed deadlock is cleared.

- Part A (one-time reclaim) remains as attested above (14 orphan compose-mcp:<sha> images removed; 76%->62%; alarm ALARM->OK). Part B now prevents recurrence in code.

Note on completion verification: the first close attempt failed because the MCP server's completion verifier inspected the main checkout's working tree (which had not fast-forwarded to the merged commit); re-running with `--ref 627faccae8df` (the merged tree) verified GREEN and signed the close.

## Surface
AWS CloudWatch, region us-east-1, account 896586841071, host `rebar-gerrit` (`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`).

## Signature
Alarm `rebar-root-disk-pressure` (metric `rebar/host:root_disk_used_percent`, threshold ≥85% Maximum, 3×5min eval) entered ALARM **6 times** during the sweep window, each self-clearing. Sampled datapoints reached 85%+ (e.g. 85.0 @ 2026-08-31T00:15Z). Currently OK (recovered 2026-08-30T17:30 PDT).

Per the alarm description, root-fs exhaustion on this box fail-closes **every LLM-Review vote** (incident 2731): Docker image/build-cache storage and the review-bot's clone tmp live on root.

## First/last seen in-window (OK→ALARM transitions, PDT)
2026-08-30 10:58, 11:53, 12:27, 15:43, 16:47 (+ prior partial). 6 OK→ALARM transitions total in window.

## Dedup
Tracking bug **3a52-2d79-320d-4fed** ("[root-disk-pressure] Root disk reaches 90%…") is **closed** (P1). Same alarm firing again = regression → this ticket links `duplicates` 3a52. Distinct from the gerrit **data**-disk item 5a05 (that is /var/gerrit; this is the 30-GiB gp3 **root** volume) and from the authorship-pack item a453.

## Severity: P2
Self-clearing flaps (no sustained exhaustion this window) but blast radius is the LLM-Review merge gate (fail-closed on exhaustion). Recurrence of a closed P1.

## Provenance
Filed by periodic ops-error sweep (window 2026-08-29T10:00 → 2026-08-30T17:36 PDT). Triage only — not root-caused.
